arguments.premise_synthesis: Savers, as lenders, earn returns below real inflation and thus lose purchasing power. Conversely, borrowers benefit because inflation makes it easier to repay debt and asset prices rise. Earners receive raises only after inflation has already occurred, so they also lose purchasing power. Owners see asset prices increase, more than compensating for cost-of-living increases.
